issue.title: Initializing default session_state value for a selectbox raises ValueError if options change
issue.body:
### Summary

If I create a [selectbox](https://docs.streamlit.io/en/stable/api.html#streamlit.selectbox) with a key that stores the selected option in session_state and the options for the selectbox changes, Streamlit raises a `ValueError` that the previous selection is not in the new options.

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```python
import streamlit as st


list_one = ("One", ("A", "B", "C"))
list_two = ("Two", ("D", "E", "F"))


if not "list" in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.list = list_two
    st.session_state.item = list_two[1][1]


st.selectbox("List", (list_one, list_two), key="list", format_func=lambda x: x[0])
st.selectbox("Item", st.session_state.list[1], key="item", format_func=lambda x: x)
```

#### Case One (Error)

1. (Optional) Choose an option from the **Item** selectbox (the second selectbox).
2. Select **One** from the **List** selectbox (the first selectbox).

If `st.session_state.item` is initialized, in this case to `E`, when the list changes (from the first selectbox), a ValueError is raised. The report is then non-operational.

```
Exception in thread ScriptRunner.scriptThread:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/threading.py", line 932, in _bootstrap_inner
    self.run()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/threading.py", line 870, in run
    self._target(*self._args, **self._kwargs)
  File "/root/.local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/script_runner.py", line 182, in _process_request_queue
    widget_states = self._session_state.as_widget_states()
  File "/root/.local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/state/session_state.py", line 447, in as_widget_states
    return self._new_widget_state.as_widget_states()
  File "/root/.local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/state/session_state.py", line 198, in as_widget_states
    states = [
  File "/root/.local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/state/session_state.py", line 201, in <listcomp>
    if self.get_serialized(widget_id)
  File "/root/.local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/state/session_state.py", line 179, in get_serialized
    serialized = metadata.serializer(item.value)
  File "/root/.local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/elements/selectbox.py", line 113, in serialize_select_box
    return index_(opt, v)
  File "/root/.local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/util.py", line 129, in index_
    raise ValueError("{} is not in iterable".format(str(x)))
ValueError: E is not in iterable
```

#### Case Two

If `st.session_state.item` is not initialized (comment out `st.session_state.item = list_two[1][1]`), then things work normally.

**Expected behavior:**

The second selectbox should work normally whether its session_state variable is initialized or not.

**Actual behavior:**

When the selectbox's session_state variable is intiialized, the selectbox raises a ValueError when the options change and the selection is not in the new options.

### Is this a regression?

Not that I'm aware of. Session state is new in Streamlit 0.84.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: Streamlit, version 0.84.2
- Python version: Python 3.8.11
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? Just pip
- OS version: Debian buster (in a python:3.8 container)
- Browser version: Safari 14.1 on macOS Mojave 10.14.6

### Additional information

None.

comments.body:
Thanks for reporting this @kinghuang!

Looks like this may be a general issue with widgets that take a list of options (I'm not entirely sure, but #3596 seems related). We'll try to look into this relatively soon (ideally within the next few weeks).
Thanks. I suspect #3600 might be related, too.

@kinghuang heads up that we're closing in on a solution to this class of issues introduced by session_state, but in the meantime our improved understanding of exactly what's going on here is enough to confirm that the root cause of this issue is the same as that of #3596, so I'm going to close this as a duplicate of the older issue. Once the fix for this class of problem is in, I'll go back through all the issues linked to that one to verify that they were indeed fixed.

Just a note that this isn't fixed. I get the same value error

```
streamlit/util.py", line 129, in index_
    raise ValueError("{} is not in iterable".format(str(x)))
```
Anyone found a workaround?

Still having the same/similar issue as Frank noted above. If only one selectbox is in the code there is no issue, when another one is inserted I get the same error:  streamlit/util.py", line 129, in index_
    raise ValueError("{} is not in iterable".format(str(x)))

I struggled for an hour with this issue on Streamlit 1.22.0 and Python 3.11.3.

My workaround: instead of "st.session_state.list" I used "st.session_state.selection" and "st.session_state.selection1" and so on as a naming convention. No idea why that works, but it works.
@vdonato this bug is clearly not fixed yet and needs to be reopened.

Removing or avoiding the input_widget name (key value) same as the session_state name solved this for me. 

```python
import streamlit as st


list_one = ("One", ("A", "B", "C"))
list_two = ("Two", ("D", "E", "F"))

if not "list" in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.list = list_two
    st.session_state.item = list_two[1][1]


st.selectbox(
  "List", 
  (list_one, list_two), 
  #key="list", 
  format_func=lambda x: x[0])
st.selectbox(
  "Item", 
  st.session_state.list[1], 
  #key="item", 
  format_func=lambda x: x)
  ```
When I remove a key I've got a DuplicateWidgetID error =(((
